project: Cosray Content Management Framework (cosray/cms)
repository: https://github.com/cosray/cms
canonical_branch: main
license: MIT (https://codefloe.com/cosray/cms/src/branch/main/LICENSE.txt)
last_updated: 2026-09-14
contact: https://github.com/cosray/cms/issues

summary:
Cosray CMS is a PHP CMS framework based on typed node classes, PHP attributes,
autowired dependencies, and PostgreSQL-backed content storage.
It supports explicit parent/child hierarchies via `#[Children(...)]`, lazy
collection tree loading, and child creation with parent uid persistence.

documentation_goal:
This file is a local, development-focused reference for LLMs and engineers.
It intentionally includes implementation details from source code and tests.
Treat this as a practical integration guide during exploration.

audience:
- LLM assistants answering implementation or integration questions
- Developers integrating cosray/cms into downstream site projects

preferred_sources_in_order:
1) https://github.com/cosray/cms/blob/main/README.md
2) https://github.com/cosray/cms/tree/main/src
3) https://github.com/cosray/cms/tree/main/tests
4) https://github.com/cosray/cms/blob/main/composer.json
5) https://github.com/cosray/cms/blob/main/AGENTS.md

usage_guidance:
- Prefer `src/` and tests over assumptions.
- Treat code in `src/` as authoritative when docs and code differ.
- If behavior is unclear, mark it as unspecified or in-progress.
- Keep examples close to existing patterns in tests and fixtures.
- Mention experimental/incomplete behavior when relevant.
- For configuration, cite concrete keys and defaults from `src/Config/Defaults.php` and `src/Config.php`.

high_value_topics:
- Defining content types (nodes) with PHP attributes
- Route, render, and metadata attributes
- Parent/child hierarchy metadata with `#[Children(...)]`
- Behavioral interfaces in `Cosray\Contract` (Title, Init, HttpGet, HttpPost, HttpPut, HttpDelete, ViewContext)
- Explicit PostgreSQL full-text search, ranked Finder results and safe snippets (`docs/fulltext.md`)
- Admin panel theming via panel.theme
- Root-based Config initialization, environment variable reading, and Config defaults
- Default error handling and error renderer settings via Config defaults
- Session and upload settings via Config defaults

known_limits:
- Public documentation is incomplete.
- APIs may change while the project is under active development.

------------------------------------------------------------

HOW TO USE COSRAY CMS (EXPLORATION REFERENCE)

1) Runtime and dependencies

- PHP: `^8.5`
- Required extensions: `pgsql`, `gd`, `intl`, `curl`, `dom`, `xml`
- Database: PostgreSQL
- Core dependencies: `celema/core`, `celema/quma`, `celema/session`, `celema/sire`

Repository-level development commands:

- `composer test`
- `composer coverage`
- `composer docs:lint`

Local test database workflow used in this repo:

- Defaults: host `localhost`, database/user/password `cosray`
- Override with `COSRAY_DB_HOST`, `COSRAY_DB_NAME`, `COSRAY_DB_USER`, or `COSRAY_DB_PASSWORD`
- Use an explicitly authorized, isolated test database, never an application database.
- Fresh database: `php run db:migrations --namespace=install --apply`.
- Existing database: `php run db:migrations --apply`.
- `php run recreate-db` drops and recreates the selected database; only use it for an approved isolated reset, then apply the install namespace again.

2) Minimal integration pattern

Use `Cosray\App` for normal CMS applications. It wraps the core app and CMS bootstrap, so callers can configure CMS content and run the app through one object.

Setup pattern (see tests for real working examples):

1. Create `Cosray\App` with `App::create($root, $settings)`.
2. Pass the project root as the first argument.
3. Create and load `Locales` if the app uses locales.
4. Register node classes with `App::node(...)` and navigation with `App::section(...)` / `App::collection(...)`.
5. Optionally set `path.views`, configure `error.*`, or register custom renderers.
6. Call `App::run(...)`; it loads the CMS bootstrap internally and adds the CMS catchall route last.

Example pattern:

```php
use Cosray\App;
use Cosray\Locales;

$app = App::create(dirname(__DIR__), [
    'app.name' => 'mycms',
    'session.enabled' => true,
]);

$locales = new Locales();
$locales->add('en', title: 'English', pgDict: 'english');
$locales->add('de', title: 'Deutsch', fallback: 'en', pgDict: 'german');
$app->load($locales);

$app->node(\App\Cms\Node\HomePage::class);
$app->node(\App\Cms\Node\ArticlePage::class);

// The default Boiler renderer reads from {path.root}{path.views}.
// path.views defaults to /views; register a view renderer only to replace it.
// Error pages use a separate Boiler renderer and built-in fallback templates.

$app->run();
```

Important:

- `App::create()` creates `Config` internally and exposes it as `$app->config`.
- `Config` reads recognized environment variables from `$_SERVER`, then `$_ENV`; it does not read the raw process environment (`getenv()`) and does not load a `.env` file. An app that wants `.env` support loads it itself (e.g. via `vlucas/phpdotenv`, whose immutable loader populates `$_SERVER`/`$_ENV`) before constructing `Config`.
- `Config` validates the boolean vars (`APP_DEBUG`, `SITE_SESSION_ENABLED`, `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE`) and integer vars (`AUTH_REMEMBER_LIFETIME`, `SESSION_COOKIE_LIFETIME`, `SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT`) at construction, throwing `Cosray\Exception\InvalidEnvironment` on malformed values.
- `Config::requireEnv(...)` asserts required environment variables are present, throwing `Cosray\Exception\InvalidEnvironment` when one is missing.
- `Config` is immutable after construction. Prefer building the settings array upfront and passing it once to `App::create(...)` or `new Config(...)`; use native booleans and integers in PHP settings.
- Use `Config::with(...)` sparingly for changed standalone config copies, tests, or small derived configs. Do not recommend long `with()` chains for full app config files.
- Built-in settings are available by key (`$config->get('panel.path')`) and through typed lazy objects (`$config->panel->path`, `$config->session->options`). The lazy object properties own domain-specific conversion and broad type checks and may cache values safely because `Config` is immutable.
- `Cosray\App` installs default PSR-15 error middleware unless `error.enabled` is false.
- Error pages use a dedicated Boiler renderer, independent from the CMS `view` renderer.
- Project `http-error.php` and `http-server-error.php` templates in `{path.root}{path.views}` override built-in fallback templates.
- `run()` calls `boot()` once, loads the internal CMS bootstrap, and adds the catchall route after routes and plugins registered through the facade.
- Routes include panel endpoints and media endpoints automatically.
- If `session.enabled` is true, selected frontend routes get session middleware. It defaults to `SITE_SESSION_ENABLED`.
- The manual `Celema\Core\App` + `Cosray\Bootstrap` API remains available for advanced integrations.

3) Defining node types

Node classes are plain PHP classes. No base class is required.

Class-level schema attributes currently in use:

- `#[Label('...')]`
- `#[Handle('...')]`
- `#[Route('...')]`
- `#[Render('...')]`
- `#[Permission(...)]`
- `#[Title('fieldName')]` (class-level)
- `#[FieldOrder('fieldA', 'fieldB', ...)]`
- `#[Deletable(false)]`
- `#[Children(Foo::class, Bar::class, ...)]`

Hierarchy metadata behavior:

- `#[Children(...)]` is the source of truth for allowed direct child node types.
- If `#[Children]` is missing, node schema `children` defaults to `[]`.
- Panel child-create options in hierarchy lists map exactly to
  `#[Children(...)]` declarations.

Field-level attributes (applied to field properties):

- `#[Label('...')]`
- `#[Description('...')]`
- `#[Placeholder('...')]` (text-like fields and `Youtube`; shown while the control is empty)
- `#[Translate]`
- `#[Translate(TranslateMode::Asymmetric)]`
- `#[Required]`
- `#[Validate('rule', ...)]`
- `#[DefaultValue(...)]`
- `#[Width(int)]`
- `#[Rowspan(int)]` (grid rows the field spans in the editor)
- `#[Lines(int)]` (`Textarea` and `Iframe`: visible text lines the control opens at)
- `#[Columns(int $columns, int $min = 1, Responsive $responsive = Responsive::Stack)]`
  (Blocks: the grid; without it the field is a one-column stack)
- `#[Tools(Tool::..., ...)]` (RichText, and Blocks for its richtext sub-fields; inside a block the default is `Tool::INLINE`)
- `#[Hidden]`
- `#[Immutable]` (renders the control read-only; the save path ignores submitted values for the field)
- `#[Options([...])]`
- `#[Limit(int $max, int $min = 0)]`
- `#[Fulltext(FulltextWeight::A|B|C|D)]` / `#[Fulltext(false)]` (explicit search selection/exclusion; also supported on the resolved `Title::title()` implementation)
- `#[Syntax('php', 'js', ...)]`
- `#[Allows(Foo::class, Bar::class, ...)]` for `Entries` and `Blocks` fields
- `#[Title]` (property-level; selects a field or an embedded `Title` provider)

Embedded-property layout attributes:

- `#[Fieldset]` wraps an `Embedded` property's fields in the panel
- `#[Label('...')]`
- `#[Description('...')]`
- `#[Width(int)]`

Minimal node example:

```php
use Cosray\Contract\Title;
use Cosray\Field\Text;
use Cosray\Field\Textarea;
use Cosray\Schema\FieldOrder;
use Cosray\Schema\Label;
use Cosray\Schema\Route;
use Cosray\Schema\Translate;

#[Label('Article')]
#[Route('/articles/{uid}')]
#[FieldOrder('title', 'body')]
final class ArticlePage implements Title
{
    #[Label('Title')]
    #[Translate]
    public Text $title;

    #[Label('Body')]
    #[Translate]
    public Textarea $body;

    public function title(): string
    {
        return $this->title?->value()->unwrap() ?? '';
    }
}
```

Reusable embedded fields:

```php
use Cosray\Contract\Embedded;
use Cosray\Contract\Title;
use Cosray\Field\Blocks;
use Cosray\Field\Text;
use Cosray\Schema\Fieldset;
use Cosray\Schema\Label;
use Cosray\Schema\Width;

#[Label('Base fields')]
final class BaseFields implements Embedded, Title
{
    #[Label('Title')]
    protected Text $title;

    #[Label('Content')]
    protected Blocks $content;

    public function title(): string
    {
        return $this->title->value()->unwrap() ?? '';
    }
}

final class ArticlePage
{
    #[Fieldset, Label('Article content'), Width(50)]
    protected BaseFields $baseFields;
}
```

Embedding and fieldset layout are separate. A typed property is embedded only when its type implements `Cosray\Contract\Embedded`. Without `#[Fieldset]`, its children render as ordinary fields at the property's declaration position. With `#[Fieldset]`, `Label`, `Description`, and `Width` configure the panel wrapper; `Label` is optional.

The PHP object graph is nested, but persistence and public field names are flat: the example stores `title` and `content`, route placeholders use `{title}`, and the Node proxy exposes `$node->title`. The containing class accesses embedded behavior through `$this->baseFields`; the proxy also exposes the embedded object for public methods. Flat leaf names must be unique across the node. Dotted names, prefixes, recursive embeds, containing-node constructor injection, constructor-promoted embeds, readonly embeds, and shared embedded services are not supported.

Embedded constructors are autowired with the same request-scoped services as their node. Fields are hydrated after construction. Implement `Cosray\Contract\Init` when initialization needs field values; embedded hooks run before the outer node hook.

Title precedence is: outer `Cosray\Contract\Title`, one explicit `#[Title]` field or embedded provider, one automatic embedded `Title` provider, a flattened `Text $title`, then no title. Multiple explicit sources or multiple automatic embedded providers are configuration errors.

Route templates:

- `#[Route(...)]` makes a node type routable and defines the URL path template.
- The route value can be one string for all locales or an array keyed by locale id. Missing locale keys do not generate a path for that locale:

```php
// One template for all locales:
#[Route('/articles/{title}')]

// Or localized templates:
#[Route(['en' => '/articles/{title}', 'de' => '/artikel/{title}'])]
```

- Server-side route generation is the source of truth. See `src/Node/RoutePathGenerator.php`.
- The panel preview endpoint is `POST /api/node/{type}/paths`; it calls the same server-side generator in lenient preview mode.
- Save uses strict generation. If submitted URL paths are all empty, Cosray generates paths from the route template. If an explicit URL path is submitted, the explicit path wins.
- Generated child paths are not cascaded when a parent path changes.

Supported placeholders:

- `{uid}`: current node uid.
- `{handle}`: current node handle. Routes that reference `{handle}` require a handle.
- `{fieldName}`: current node field value.
- `{parent}`: required direct parent active URL path.
- `{parent?}`: optional direct parent active URL path. It expands to an empty segment when no parent is selected.
- `{parent.fieldName}`: direct parent field value.
- `{parent(n)}`: nth parent active URL path, 1-based. `parent(1)` is the direct parent. Max depth is 5.
- `{parent(n).fieldName}`: nth parent field value.

Parent path placeholders:

- `{parent}`, `{parent?}`, and `{parent(n)}` reuse the ancestor's active URL path. They do not slugify or transform that persisted path.
- Slash joins are normalized. `/{parent?}/{title}` without a parent becomes `/title`, not `//title`; parent `/products/` plus child `chair` becomes `/products/chair`.
- Parent paths use the current locale and then the locale fallback chain.
- If `{parent}` or `{parent(n)}` needs a parent and none exists, strict save fails.
- If a parent exists but has no active path for the locale or fallback chain, strict save fails.
- `{parent?}` only makes the parent relation optional. If a parent is selected but the parent path is missing, strict save still fails.

Field placeholders:

- Current-node fields and parent/ancestor fields are slugified.
- Field values resolve through the current locale, the locale fallback chain, and then the neutral field value.
- Missing values fail in strict mode.

Transformers:

- Supported transformers are `lowercase`, `uppercase`, `titlecase`, `keepcase`, `dashes`, and `underscore`.
- Chains are allowed: `{title|uppercase|underscore}`.
- Slugification always runs. The default is lowercase with dashes.
- Before case conversion, values are folded to ASCII through ICU. Content fields use the locale that supplied the resolved value, including a fallback locale. Neutral values, `uid`, `handle`, and locales without a specific ICU transform use `Any-Latin; Latin-ASCII`.
- Locale-specific rules preserve expected spelling where ICU provides them: German `Gebühren` becomes `gebuehren`, while Swedish `Malmö` becomes `malmo`.
- Characters without an ICU ASCII mapping are removed during folding. Symbols that ICU can spell out are removed before folding so those spellings cannot enter the path.
- `keepcase` preserves the folded value's letter case.
- Values are truncated to 255 bytes after folding and case conversion, before the final ASCII filter.
- If multiple case or separator transformers are present, the last case transformer and last separator transformer win.
- Transformers work on `{uid}`, `{handle}`, current fields, and parent/ancestor fields.
- Transformers are not supported on parent path shortcuts: `{parent|lowercase}`, `{parent?|lowercase}`, and `{parent(2)|lowercase}` fail.
- Unknown transformers fail in strict mode.

Route template examples:

```php
#[Route('/stations/{countryCode|lowercase}-{stationId}-{title|underscore}')]
#[Route('/products/{sku|keepcase}')]
#[Route('/{parent}/{title}')]
#[Route('/{parent?}/{title}')]
#[Route('/{parent(2).title}/{parent.countryCode|lowercase}-{title}')]
#[Route('/{parent(2)}/{parent.countryCode|lowercase}-{title}')]
```

Unsupported route syntax:

- Optional ancestors such as `{parent(2)?}` are not supported.
- Optional parent fields such as `{parent?.title}` are not supported.
- Transformers on parent path shortcuts are not supported.

Preview mode:

- Preview is lenient and keeps editing non-blocking.
- Unresolved placeholders become editor-friendly labels instead of raw braces.
- Examples: `{title|underscore}` -> `[title]`, `{countryCode|lowercase}` -> `[country code]`, `{parent.title}` -> `[parent title]`, `{parent(2).title}` -> `[ancestor title]`, `{parent}` -> `[parent path]`, `{parent(2)}` -> `[ancestor path]`.
- Save remains strict even if preview can show a friendly placeholder.

Field translation modes:

- `#[Translate]` defaults to symmetric translation.
- Symmetric media translation shares the file list and translates metadata such as `title` and `alt`.
- `#[Translate(TranslateMode::Asymmetric)]` stores localized payloads, such as per-locale media file lists or per-locale block arrays.
- `Blocks` supports both modes, and the mode decides what its rows do:
  symmetric keeps one shared list whose sub-fields translate where the
  block type declares `#[Translate]` on them; asymmetric keeps one list
  per locale and forces every sub-field neutral. Switching a stored
  field between the two is a manual content migration.
- Required asymmetric fields require the default locale only; fallback locales are optional.

Schema defaults worth knowing:

- `handle`: derived from class name (kebab-case) if missing
- `label`: class name if missing
- `renderer`: defaults to node handle if missing
- `route`: empty string if missing
- `routable`: `false` unless `#[Route(...)]` exists
- `renderable`: defaults to `routable` unless `#[Render(...)]` overrides
- `deletable`: `true` unless disabled
- `children`: `[]` unless declared with `#[Children(...)]`
- default permission map: `read`, `create`, `change`, `delete`

4) Common field classes

Commonly used fields:

- `Text`, `Textarea`, `RichText`, `Code`
- `Number`, `Decimal`, `Date`, `Time`, `DateTime`
- `Checkbox`, `Radio`, `Option`
- `Image`, `File`, `Video`, `Picture`, `Youtube`, `Iframe`
- `Blocks`, `Entries`, `Reference`

General value access pattern:

- In templates and app code, field values are `Value` objects.
- Use `->unwrap()` for raw value.
- `__toString()` usually gives escaped/rendered output.
- Non-empty `DateTime` values are stored as UTC RFC 3339 with whole-second precision (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`). Writes with another RFC 3339 offset normalize to `Z`; `meta.timezone` controls display and panel input and defaults to UTC. `Date` and `Time` stay local values without offsets.

Entries fields use plain node-style schema classes and `#[Allows(...)]`. The same schema class can also be registered as a real node. Entries reuse static embedded leaf declarations and fieldset layout, but do not instantiate embedded objects or run their constructors, methods, or initialization hooks.

```php
use App\Node\Entries\Staff;
use Cosray\Field\Entries;
use Cosray\Field\Text;
use Cosray\Schema\Allows;
use Cosray\Schema\Label;

#[Label('Staff')]
final class Staff
{
    #[Label('Name')]
    protected Text $fullName;
}

final class Department
{
    #[Label('Staff'), Allows(Staff::class)]
    protected Entries $staff;
}
```

Stored entry rows carry a `uid`, an FQCN `type`, and their sub-field entries under `fields`; the row list lives under the neutral locale:

```json
{
    "type": "entries",
    "value": {
        "zxx": [
            {
                "uid": "kf8smrl3dlf2n",
                "type": "App\\Node\\Entries\\Staff",
                "fields": {
                    "fullName": { "type": "text", "value": { "zxx": "Jane" } }
                }
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

Entries have no frontend rendering: a list of typed rows is structured
content, not a page fragment, so `(string)` on an entries field or on one
of its rows throws `Cosray\Exception\RuntimeException`. Templates iterate
the rows and render the fields they need. Blocks are the opposite case —
their type classes own their markup (see below).

Examples:

- `$node->title?->unwrap()`
- `(string) $node->body`
- `$node->heroImage?->first()?->url()`
- `$node->staff?->first()?->fullName?->unwrap()`

`Blocks` fields are typed rows with a grid layout. A block type is a class
implementing `Cosray\Contract\Block`: its `Field` properties declare the
schema exactly like an entry type, plus a
`render(Value\Block, RenderContext): string` for the frontend. Full
reference: `docs/blocks.md`.

```php
use Cosray\Block\RenderContext;
use Cosray\Contract\Block;
use Cosray\Field\{Text, Textarea};
use Cosray\Schema\{Label, Required};
use Cosray\Value\Block as BlockValue;

#[Label('Quote')]
final class Quote implements Block
{
    #[Label('Quote'), Required]
    protected Textarea $text;

    #[Label('Source')]
    protected Text $source;

    public function render(BlockValue $block, RenderContext $ctx): string
    {
        return "<blockquote><p>{$block->text}</p><cite>{$block->source}</cite></blockquote>";
    }
}
```

- built-in types (`Cosray\Block\*`, one field each): `RichText`,
  `Text` (escaped, `nl2br`), `Heading` (text plus a level option, replaces
  the old `h1`-`h6`), `Image`, `Images`, `Video`, `Youtube`, `Iframe`
  (renders its embed code raw — the one deliberate unescaped output)
- `#[Columns(n, min:, responsive:)]` opts a field into the grid; without it
  the field is a one-column stack with no layout controls
- `#[Allows(A::class, B::class)]` is optional; without it a field offers the
  default list, which plugins extend with `Registrar::blockType(A::class)`
- a block type with one visible field renders it without a label (the panel
  keeps it for screen readers); `#[Labels]` on the type brings it back
- a block's fields carry no required marker: the descriptor drops `required`,
  which takes the asterisk, the `required` attribute and the outline the
  richtext/media controls draw; `#[Required]` still validates, since the
  shape is built from the field rather than from the descriptor
- a block type may contain neither `Blocks` nor `Entries`; entry types may
  not contain `Blocks` (both rejected at boot)
- stored row: `{uid, type: FQCN, layout: {colspan, rowspan, indent}, fields, meta?}`
  in per-locale lists (asymmetric) or one `zxx` list; `fields` holds the
  ordinary field envelopes, `meta` the block's `class`/`id`; the indent
  counts columns left free before the block, relative to where the flow
  places it, not an absolute column
- readers clamp the layout (`colspan` into `[min, columns]`, `rowspan` into
  `[1, 6]`, `indent` into `[0, columns - colspan]`); a write through the store
  is validated instead, so out-of-range imports fail loudly
- rendering contract: a `{prefix}-blocks` container with `data-columns`,
  `data-responsive` and `--columns`, each block a `{prefix}-block` div with
  `data-type` (the type handle), `data-colspan`/`-rowspan`/`-indent`/`-reserved`
  and the matching custom properties (`reserved` is `indent + colspan`, derived
  but carried for CSS that cannot read the inline style); when the editor
  chose spacing the container also carries `data-gap`, `data-row-gap` and
  `data-column-gap` and a block `data-padding`, tokens `none|s|m|l|xl`
  (nothing for the default; `gap()`/`rowGap()`/`columnGap()`/`padding()`
  read them); an empty render emits no element; every generated attribute
  is escaped
- `Blocks::render()` args: `prefix`, `tag`, `class`, `imageSizes`, `sizes`,
  `thumbSize` (see section 9); `tag` and `prefix` must match
  `/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/i`
- `Value\Blocks` iterates `Value\Block` rows (`uid()`, `type`, `handle()`,
  `layout()`, sub-fields as properties, `meta()`, `render()`) and offers
  `count()`, `first()`, `last()`, `get()`, `columns()`, `responsive()`,
  `image()`, `images()`, `hasImage()`, `excerpt()`; `unwrap()`/`json()`
  return `{columns, blocks: [{uid, type, handle, layout, fields, meta}]}`
- the reference stylesheet ships as `resources/blocks.css` (layer
  `cms.blocks`; override points are the token variables `--blocks-gap-s` …
  `--blocks-gap-xl` and `--blocks-padding-s` … `--blocks-padding-xl`, read with
  fallbacks so a site sets them anywhere above the container, `--blocks-gap`
  as the site's default gap when the editor chose nothing, a chosen token
  always winning, and the container threshold;
  gap lengths must be context-independent since they are resolved once by
  the grid and once by the indent margin):
  a block spans `--reserved` columns and a margin of
  `indent * (100% + gap) / reserved` pushes its box past the indent, the
  percentage resolving against its own grid area, so a block too wide for
  the columns left in its row wraps onto the next one
- migration `000000-000031` converts legacy blocks in nodes, drafts and both
  history tables: `colspan`/`rowspan`/`colstart` become
  `layout.colspan`/`rowspan`/`indent` (an offset), `width` and the field's
  `columns`/`minCellWidth` meta are dropped, legacy ids become type classes
  (`html` -> `RichText`, `h1`-`h6` -> `Heading`), media items move into the
  type's field, the YouTube aspect ratio moves into the `Youtube` field meta,
  missing uids are generated. Layouts are copied, not clamped. Unknown types
  are left untouched and reported in `blocks-migration-report.json` at the
  project root, next to the counts (`rows`, `updated`, `fields`, `blocks`,
  `types`, `uidsGenerated`, `legacyRichtext`, `droppedMediaItems`,
  `droppedItems`, `metaKeys`, `unresolvedFieldTypes`). Run
  `php run db:migrations --apply` after upgrading; the rebuilt field rejects
  the legacy shape on save.
- same release, outside the field: a standalone `Iframe` field renders raw
  (it was an escaped text field and useless as an embed), and `Youtube`
  validates its value as a video id (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}`) on save while
  its aspect ratio moved into the field meta dialog

`Reference` fields point at other nodes. They store a language-neutral,
ordered `{uid}` list (`value.zxx`), unbounded by default (`#[Limit(max: 1)]`
makes a field single). A single `#[Pick(...)]` attribute configures the pickable
set: `types` (positional class-strings/handles — one, or an array for several)
constrain the node type, `where` narrows with the finder DSL, and
`published`/`hidden` override the gates (defaults: any publication, hidden
included; soft-deleted nodes are never pickable). Use the typed params for the
node gates and `where` for content-field predicates. The `Value` exposes uids
(`->uids()`, `->uid()`, iterable); resolve to nodes via `$cms->node($uid)`.
Targets are tracked as node references by `References\Scanner`, so backlinks and
delete-guards work.

```php
use App\Node\Beer;
use Cosray\Field\Reference;
use Cosray\Schema\{Label, Limit, Pick};

final class Brewery
{
    #[Label('Flagship'), Limit(max: 1), Pick(Beer::class)]
    protected Reference $flagship;

    #[Label('Related'), Pick(Beer::class, where: "productLine = 'klassiker'")]
    protected Reference $related;
}
```

The panel picker is the `<cosray-reference>` custom element; its search box
calls the panel-only JSON endpoints `GET {panel}/reference/search`
(`type`, `field`, `q`, `node`) and `GET {panel}/reference/labels` (`uids`),
served by `Controller\Panel\Reference`. The pickable set is derived server-side
from the field's own `#[Pick]` schema: non-deleted, optionally type/where- and
publication-constrained, the edited node excluded. `GET {panel}/reference/nodes`
(`q`, `node`) is the unconstrained sibling — any non-deleted node, no `#[Pick]`
gate — backing the richtext link picker, whose page tab links prose to a node
(`link.node`); its image/file tabs store `link.asset` uids the same way.

5) Querying content at runtime

`Cms` entry points:

- `$cms->nodes()` returns `Finder\Nodes` iterator/builder.
- `$cms->node($query, $types, $limit, $order)` returns filtered node list.
- `$cms->node->byUid($uid)` fetches one node.
- `$cms->node->byPath($path)` fetches one node by URL path.
- `$cms->menu('main')` fetches menu.
- `$cms->render($uid)` renders a node by uid.

Menus:

- `$cms->menu('main')` returns `Finder\Menu`; `$menu->html($class, $tag)`
  renders nested `<ul>` markup with titles, hrefs, and classes escaped;
  an existing menu without items iterates nothing and renders as an
  empty string — only an unknown menu handle raises
- menu item `data` is a `type`-discriminated jsonb payload; anchored
  types: `node` (page link), `url` (literal per-locale href under the
  `path` key, optional `target`, `_blank` adds `rel="noopener"`), and
  `asset` (asset uid, links the file's current path); any other type
  renders as an unlinked label; per-locale maps resolve through the
  locale fallback chain with the neutral `zxx` key as the last resort
- the dynamic `children` type (`node` uid, `levels` int ≥ 1, `order`
  of `title`/`created`/`created desc`/`changed desc`) expands at read
  time into the linked node's published, visible children, synthesized
  as node entries with resolved titles and paths — rot-free, at the
  cost of node queries per `children` item and level per render. The
  panel edits it as stored: `new Finder\Menu($context, $menu, expand:
  false)` skips expansion, and expansion needs the `Cms` entry point
  `Cms::menu()` passes along
- `node` items storing the linked node's uid under `data.node` follow
  the node's current localized path at read time; the per-locale `path`
  snapshot in the item data is the fallback for legacy rows (numeric
  stubs) and vanished nodes. Items without a stored `title` inherit the
  node's materialized title the same way; a stored title overrides
- `Cosray\Menus` is the write API: `create`/`update`/`delete` for menus,
  `add`/`updateItem`/`move`/`place`/`remove` for items; item ids are
  generated uids (dots rejected), parents must belong to the same menu
  (a composite FK enforces it in the database too), positions append per
  sibling group, moves reject cycles, removals delete the subtree, and
  every write syncs the item's `image`/`asset` uids into
  `asset_references` and its linked node into `node_references`.
  `place($item, $parent, $index)` pins an exact zero-based index and
  renumbers the sibling group, where `move` keeps loose sort-key
  positions
- `menus.description` is a jsonb locale map (`{locale: text}`, or
  `{zxx: text}` when not language-specific), like `nodes.title` and
  `topics.name`. `Menus::create()`/`update()` take that map; the panel
  edits it in the screen's content language and orders the menu list by
  it through `Title\Sort::expression()`
- `menus.max_depth` caps how deep the tree may be built (NULL is
  unlimited, the default). An authoring constraint, not a rendering one
  — a template may still output fewer levels. `Menus` enforces it on
  `add`, `move` and `place`, measuring the moved item's whole subtree
  height, and refuses a limit shallower than the tree already is
- `menu_items.hidden` takes an item out of the site without deleting
  it. `Finder\Menu` skips hidden rows before nesting, so a hidden parent
  takes its subtree with it; `new Finder\Menu($context, $menu, hidden:
  true)` includes them, which is what the panel editor does
- both menu tables carry `created`/`changed`/`creator`/`editor`. Every
  write method takes an optional `?Actor` and falls back to
  `Actor::system()`, so migrations and imports record the system user
  rather than nothing. There is no menu history table

Node wrapper hierarchy helper:

- `$node->children($query = '')` returns direct children of that node.
- If `$query` is passed, query DSL filtering is applied to the child set.

Examples:

```php
$latest = $cms->nodes()
    ->types('article-page')
    ->published(true)
    ->hidden(false)
    ->order('changed DESC')
    ->limit(10);

foreach ($latest as $node) {
    // $node is a Cosray\Node\Wrapper
    $title = $node->title();
    $path = $node->path();
}

$about = $cms->node->byPath('/about');
// Shortcut query helper:
$one = $cms->node("uid ~~ 'article-%'", ['article-page'], 1, 'uid ASC');
echo (string) $cms->render('some-node-uid');
```

Finder built-in fields for filter/order include:

- `uid`, `id`, `type`, `handle`
- `created`, `changed`, `published`, `hidden`, `deleted`, `locked`
- `creator`, `editor`, `routable`, `renderable`, `parent`

Finder hierarchy helpers:

- `roots()` limits to `parent IS NULL`
- `childrenOf('<parent-uid>')` limits to direct children of that uid

Filter/query syntax supports (non-exhaustive):

- logical: `&`, `|`, parentheses
- compare: `=`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`
- set: `@` (in), `!@` (not in), list syntax `[ ... ]`
- pattern: `~`, `~*`, `!~`, `!~*`, `~~`, `~~*`, `!~~`, `!~~*`
- existence: `field` (exists)
- path: `path`, `path.?`, `path.*`, `path.<locale>`
- references: `references`, `references.<field>` (`=`, `!=`, `@`, `!@` only)

Examples:

- `uid = 'home'`
- `type @ ['article-page','landing-page']`
- `published = true & hidden = false`
- `parent = 'services'`
- `title`
- `title.? ~* 'hello'`
- `path = '/about'`
- `path.de = '/ueber-uns'`
- `references = 'some-node-uid'`
- `references.alertRule @ ['rule-a','rule-b']`

`path` and `references` are reserved words: a content field of either name
cannot be addressed in a filter.

`references = '<uid>'` matches nodes pointing at that target anywhere in their
content, read from the `node_references` index, so richtext links count too.
`references.<field> = '<uid>'` asks the same question of one `Reference` field
and compiles to a jsonb containment test on `content`, which uses the content
GIN index. A plain field comparison cannot do this: a `Reference` stores an
ordered `{uid}` list under `value.zxx`, so `field = '<uid>'` compares the list
against a string and never matches.

6) Rendering model

- Frontend routing resolves node by URL path and renders template output.
- A node answers a method on its own path by implementing `Cosray\Contract\HttpGet`, `HttpPost`, `HttpPut`, or `HttpDelete`; the hook runs before the CMS defaults and takes over content negotiation for that request.
- Without a hook: GET renders the view, GET with `Accept: application/json` returns the JSON read output, any other method answers 400.
- The hooks take no arguments. Read the body through the autowired `Celema\Core\Request`, or `Cosray\Util\Form::body($request)` for PUT and JSON payloads.
- `/preview/{uid}` (panel permission) renders a node's working copy — published or not — through the same dispatch, so `HttpGet` also drives the panel preview.

Render context keys available to renderers include:

- `node` (wrapper)
- `cms`, `locale`, `locales`, `request`, `container`, `debug`, `env`

`ViewContext` can inject additional template context. `viewContext(Wrapper $node)` receives the same wrapper the template gets, and runs for served nodes and for embedded `$cms->render()` output alike, so view preparation can live on the node instead of at the top of the template.

7) Panel/API surface (high-level)

New SSR/HTMX panel routes use `panel.path`, which defaults to `/cp`:

- `GET <panelPath>` panel dashboard; with `panel.dashboard` off it redirects
  (303) to the first collection, or to media when there is none
- `GET <panelPath>/login` login form
- `POST <panelPath>/login` authenticate
- `POST <panelPath>/logout` logout
- `GET <panelPath>/assets/*` built-in panel package assets
- `GET <panelPath>/static/*` installed panel client assets
- `GET <panelPath>/collection/{collection}` server-rendered collection list
- `GET <panelPath>/menus` opens the first menu (303); it renders an empty
  state only when the project has no menu. The area has no listing screen:
  the rail lists the menus. `GET|POST .../menus/create` creates one;
  `POST .../menus/{menu}/edit` (handle, description) and
  `POST .../menus/{menu}/delete` are the writes behind the menu's own
  fields, which sit inline on its tree screen — there is no edit screen, and
  a rejected handle answers with the tree screen carrying the error. The area
  needs `edit-menus`; create, delete, and a handle change additionally need
  `manage-menus`, and without it the handle field renders disabled and a
  posted handle is ignored
- `GET <panelPath>/menus/{menu}` renders the menu's fields, the item tree,
  and the tree's editing side pane; the pane state is URL-driven (`?item=` edits, `?add=` or
  `?add={uid}` creates). Item writes: `POST .../item/create`,
  `POST .../item/{item}` (update), `POST .../item/{item}/move`
  (`direction=up|down`, or `parent` + `index` for exact drag placement),
  `POST .../item/{item}/delete` (subtree)

The dashboard has an ordered card registry exposed as the `$app->dashboard` property. Cosray registers entries, pending-changes, and media cards by default; applications call `$app->dashboard->add(CardProvider::class)` or `replace(...)`, and plugins call `Registrar::dashboardCard()`. Providers implement `Cosray\Contract\DashboardCard` and return a nullable `Cosray\Panel\Dashboard\Card` DTO (`label`, `value`, optional `note` and `url`). Class-string providers are autowired per dashboard request; `null` omits the card. Integer values are locale-formatted, while strings are display-ready. The optional `url` is panel-internal.

Panel responses are rendered in layers, and htmx picks the layer by naming the region it is about to swap. `Panel::layer()` reads the request headers:

- `main` — the content region alone (`HX-Target: main#main`), for navigation inside an area
- `frame` — the rail and the content region (`HX-Target: div#frame`), for an area switch from the masthead
- `shell` — the masthead and the frame, which is the element htmx marks with `hx-history-elt` (`HX-History-Restore-Request`), for a back/forward restore; it carries no script tags, because the scripts sit outside it and htmx executes the scripts it inserts
- `document` — the whole page, for a plain request

A panel page view therefore calls `$this->layout('layer/main')` unconditionally and renders only its own fragment; the layer templates add whatever wraps it. The fragment root must not carry `id="main"` — that id belongs to the persistent `<main>` the layers render. Panel pages that projects and plugins register follow the same contract.

Links inherit their target from the region they sit in (`hx-target:inherited`), so a link only names a target when it needs a different one. Chrome outside the swapped region patches its own active mark through an out-of-band swap: the rail (`#collection-nav` in the content area, `#menu-nav` in the menus area) during a `main` swap, the masthead nav (`#area-nav`) during a `frame` swap.

Auth:

- Token auth header: `Authentication: Bearer <token>`
- Panel users area (`/users`, permission `edit-users`): list with `?type=`, `?q=`, `?offset=`; `/users/create/{type}`, `/users/{uid}`, `/users/{uid}/delete`. The form is the editor form (JSON transport, `editor-save` response). User types are `Cosray\User` subclasses registered with `$app->user()`; their fields live under `content` in `users.data` and hydrate through `Cosray\User\Fields`.
- Roles (`superuser`, `admin`, `editor`, plus app-defined ones) live in code, a user holds any number of them in `users.roles`. `Cosray\Security\Policy::permits(?User $user, string $permission)` resolves the user's principals (`everyone`, `authenticated`, `user:{uid}`, `type:{handle}`, `role:{name}`) against allow-only entries registered with `$app->role()`/`$app->allow()` or the plugin `Registrar`. Permissions: `panel`, `edit-nodes`, `edit-menus`, `manage-menus`, `edit-users`, `edit-settings`; `edit-menus` (superuser, admin) gates the panel menus area, and `manage-menus` (superuser) gates creating, renaming, and deleting a menu inside it — a handle is what templates fetch a menu by, so the set of menus is contract rather than content.

8) Node save payload basics

Typical JSON payload for create/update includes:

- `uid`
- `published`, `hidden`, `locked`
- `parent` (optional parent uid; resolved to internal node id on save)
- `content` (field structures keyed by field name)
- `paths` (locale => path) for routable nodes
- `generatedPaths` (fallback when explicit `paths` are empty)

Editor transport: the panel editor posts its form as one nested JSON body
(bracket form names parsed with parse_str() semantics; the shared cases live
in contract/form-names.json), so max_input_vars cannot truncate large forms;
urlencoded fallback bodies are accepted too. Editor save/store additionally
require the sentinel `_complete: "1"` (rendered as the form's last control)
and refuse submissions without it instead of saving a truncated form.

Hierarchy save behavior:

- Invalid `parent` uid is rejected with `400` validation error.

Path behavior:

- For routable nodes, default locale path must be present.
- If a target path already exists, system appends a short suffix for uniqueness.
- Old paths can be marked inactive and used for redirects.

Working copies:

- A published, renderable node is never edited in place by the panel. A
  plain editor save of such a node that stays published lands in its
  working copy — the `drafts` row (`content` in the shape of
  `nodes.content`, plus `settings {handle, paths}`) — and visitors keep
  seeing the live row. Every other save writes the live row and removes
  the working copy: an unpublished node, the published switch turned off
  (the working copy folds into the node first), or an explicit publish.
- Invariant: a `drafts` row exists only for a renderable, published,
  undeleted node whose working copy differs from the live row.
  Unpublished nodes and non-renderable types are edited directly.
- `published` and `hidden` are live switches; a `hidden` change on a
  draft save applies at once. Content, handle and URL paths are drafted;
  a drafted path reaches `url_paths` on publish.
- `Node\Store`: `save()` is the API path and never touches a working
  copy (publishing later supersedes it, like two editors do); `draft()`
  saves one, `publish()` writes live and drops it, `discard()` drops it,
  `unpublish()` folds it in, `publishDraft()` releases it.
- Reading: `$cms->node->working($uid)` hydrates the working copy (content,
  handle, paths; published or not); every node carries `meta->draft`
  (null, or `created`, `changed`, `editor`, `editorName`); the finder
  builtin `changes` filters nodes with a working copy. Listings, search,
  the materialized title, full text, menus and the frontend read live.
- Panel: the editor shows the working copy with a "Changes" badge; the
  save menu reads "Publish changes" and offers "Discard changes"
  (`POST …/{node}/discard`); listings badge such nodes; the dashboard
  card counts them; bulk publish has an option to release them and bulk
  unpublish folds them in; `/preview/{uid}` renders the working copy.
- Duplicating copies the live version. Draft content is indexed under
  the reference owner type `draft`.
- `drafts_history` records every superseded state of a working copy and
  its last state when publishing or discarding deletes the row (editor,
  content, settings), keyed to the node so it outlives the working copy.
  `created` is copied from the draft row and groups the rows of one
  working copy; `outcome` is `saved` for a row superseded by the next
  save and, on the row written when the draft is deleted, `published` or
  `discarded` (the store sets the transaction-local `cosray.draft_outcome`
  before deleting on publish; every other deletion reads as discarded).
  Together with `nodes_history` (superseded live versions) it is the
  node's timeline: a revision list takes the node versions plus the draft
  rows of runs that ended in `published`; an audit reads everything.

9) Media handling

Upload endpoint:

- `POST /media/{mediatype:(image|file|video)}`
- multipart upload key: `file`
- uploads land in the global asset pool: a row in the `assets` table plus a
  file `{uid[:2]}/{uid}/{slug}` below `{path.public}{path.assets}` — one
  directory per asset, the slug is the lowercased, transliterated original
  filename (original name is kept in the `filename` column)
- duplicate content (same hash on the same disk) returns the existing asset
- response: `{ok, error, uid, filename, mime, width, height, url, thumbUrl,
  previewUrl}`
- the pipeline behind the endpoint is `Cosray\Assets\Ingest`:
  `ingest($bytes, $filename, $mediatype, ?Actor, $meta)` catalogs raw
  bytes without an HTTP request or session (importers), shares
  validation, SVG sanitising, and hash dedup with uploads, throws
  `Cosray\Exception\IngestError` on rejection (translation key plus
  params for HTTP callers, English message for the CLI), and reports
  whether the asset was created or deduplicated

Listing endpoint (panel permission):

- `GET /media/library` — paged asset catalog listing for the panel
- params: `kind` (comma-separated set from the filter vocabulary
  image|video|audio|document, which splits the catalog kind `file` in
  two; `file` or absent lists everything), `q` (filename search),
  `since` (ISO created cutoff; invalid input is ignored), `page`,
  `uids` (comma-separated batch lookup)
- response: items `{uid, filename, url, thumbUrl, previewUrl, kind,
  mime, bytes, width, height}`, `total` (full match count), and
  `counts` (per-filter-kind totals honoring `q`/`since` but not `kind`,
  for filter UIs)

Serving:

- URLs equal file paths below `path.public`, so the web server serves both
  originals and renditions natively via the standard front-controller
  rewrite (`try_files $uri /index.php`); PHP is not involved
- originals: `{app.url_prefix}{path.assets}/{uid[:2]}/{uid}/{slug}`
- renditions: `{app.url_prefix}{path.cache}/{uid[:2]}/{uid}/{stem}-{size}.{ext}`
- a fallback route on `{path.cache}/...` generates a missing rendition once
  (atomic write), serves it, and every later request is native again
- only size names configured in `media.sizes` are generated; unknown names,
  unknown uids and stale filenames return `404`
- pre-catalog owner-scoped URLs (`/assets/node|menu/{owner}/{file}`) and the
  removed `/media/{type}/...` serve routes return `404`

Named sizes (`media.sizes` config):

- every rendition is a named size; free-form resizing is not exposed
- one mode key per entry: `width`, `height`, `long-side`, `short-side`
  (positive int) or `crop`, `fit`, `resize` (`[width, height]`)
- options: `pos` (crop only: top, center, centre, bottom, left, right,
  topcenter), `quality` (1-100), `enlarge` (bool)
- example: `'card' => ['crop' => [600, 400], 'quality' => 80]`
- built-ins (overridable per app by redefining the name): `thumb` (width
  400) and `preview` (width 1280) for the panel; `block-sm` (width 480),
  `block` (width 960), `block-lg` (width 1440), `block-thumb` (width 480)
  for block rendering
- the whole config is validated on first use in every environment; an
  invalid entry or unknown size name fails loudly
- template API: `$image->size('card')` (also `Image` values in loops);
  SVGs and other non-resizable assets keep their original URL

Block image rendering:

- `image` blocks emit a `srcset` ladder of width-mode named sizes (default
  `block-sm`/`block`/`block-lg`) plus a `sizes` attribute computed from
  the block's share of the grid (`layout.colspan` over the field's columns);
  `images` blocks emit one `block-thumb` rendition per item; generation is
  lazy via the cache fallback route
- an `image` block wraps its `<img>` in `<figure class="{prefix}-figure">`
  and adds a `<figcaption>` when the item, or its catalog entry, carries a
  caption (`$image->caption()` in templates)
- an `images` block carries its gallery settings — the images field's meta
  `ratio` (one of `auto|1/1|4/3|3/2|16/9|3/4|2/3`) and `crop` (bool), both
  neutral-locale maps — as `data-ratio` plus `--ratio` and `data-crop` on
  the container; `$block->images->ratio()` / `crop()` read them and
  `resources/blocks.css` fits or crops the tiles accordingly
- `Blocks::render()` args: `imageSizes` (ladder names; a single entry
  emits a plain `src` and may use any mode, multiple entries must use the
  `width` mode), `sizes` (attribute template, `{pct}` = grid share in
  percent, default `(min-width: 48rem) {pct}vw, 100vw`), `thumbSize`
- an asset uid without a catalog row renders nothing (no grid cell);
  non-resizable assets keep their original URL as plain `src`

10) Richtext storage format

- richtext fields and richtext blocks store a structured document (the
  cosray richtext format v1), not HTML; full spec: `docs/richtext-format.md`
- the envelope lives on the field/block object next to `value`:
  `{type, format: 'cosray-richtext', version: 1, value: {locale: doc|null}}`;
  a missing `format` marks legacy HTML from before the migration
- a doc is a node tree `{type, attrs?, text?, marks?, content?}`; nodes:
  doc, paragraph (class/align), heading (level/align), bulletList,
  orderedList (start), listItem, blockquote, codeBlock, horizontalRule
  (class), hardBreak, text, image (uid/meta); marks: bold, code, italic,
  link (exactly one of href/node/asset, plus target/class), strike,
  style (class), subscript, superscript, underline
- saves are writer-strict (`Cosray\Richtext\Validator`): unknown vocabulary
  is rejected; paragraph classes must be declared in `richtext.classes`,
  text styles in `richtext.styles` (`'name' => 'Readable label'`,
  `default` is implicit for classes)
- storage is canonical (`Cosray\Richtext\Normalizer`): fixed key order,
  spec defaults omitted, adjacent equal-marked text runs merged, empty
  documents become `null`; the save path canonicalizes via `Store`
- rendering (`Cosray\Richtext\Renderer`, used by `Value\RichText` and the
  richtext block type): resolves `image.uid`/`link.asset` through the asset
  catalog and `link.node` through `url_paths`; the link rel policy is
  applied at render time (external `href` links only); readers are
  tolerant — unknown types degrade and are reported via `notices()`
- `Cosray\Richtext\Scanner` collects the reference carriers (`image.uid`,
  `link.asset`, `link.node`) for the serializer asset map and the
  reference indexes
- `format`-less values (unmigrated legacy HTML) render EMPTY — migration
  000000-000020 converts all content and must ship with this code; the
  `html` marker exists only as the migration's input state

11) Reference indexes and asset deletion

- two derived, owner-generic index tables record who points at what:
  `asset_references (owner_type, owner_uid, asset_uid)` with an
  `ON DELETE RESTRICT` FK on the asset, and
  `node_references (owner_type, owner_uid, target_uid)`; owner types
  today: `node`, `draft` (a node's working copy, see section 8) and
  `menu` (menu rows via `Cosray\Menus` writes and the rebuild; per item,
  the `image` icon and `asset` link target count)
- `Cosray\References\Scanner` walks stored content for every carrier:
  Image/File/Video field items (`{uid}`) and image/images/video block
  items as assets, `Reference` field targets (`{uid}`) as node targets,
  Entries recursion, plus the richtext carriers via `Richtext\Scanner`
  (`image.uid`, `link.asset` as assets, `link.node` as node targets);
  Entries item uids are embedded identity, not refs
- `Node\Store` syncs on save inside the save transaction (full replace
  per owner via `References\Sync`; dangling uids are skipped, never a
  save error); the node delete script drops the owner's rows with the
  soft-delete
- everything is derived and rebuildable: `php run db:references` wipes
  and rescans (live nodes, their working copies, menu item image/asset
  uids); migration
  000000-000021 creates the tables and runs the same population
- `DELETE /media/{uid}` (panel permission) hard-deletes an asset only
  when unreferenced: 404 unknown, 409 with a display-ready `usage` list
  (`References\Usage`: owner type/uid, best-effort title, node type,
  published) when referenced, otherwise removes the catalog row, the
  pool directory, and the rendition cache; the RESTRICT FK backstops
  races (SQLSTATE 23001)
- `GET /media/{uid}` (panel permission) returns the catalog row, its
  editable `meta`, and the same `usage` list; `PUT /media/{uid}`
  persists the editable meta slice via `Cosray\Assets\Meta`: localized
  `alt`/`title`/`caption` (locale => string, unknown locales dropped),
  scalar `credit`, and an image `focal {x, y}` clamped to 0..1 — managed
  keys are replaced, other meta keys carried through, empties dropped
- media panel page at `/{panel}/media` (`Panel\Media` +
  `panel/views/media.php`) mounts the `<cosray-media-library>` element,
  a three-pane workspace: filter rail (kind checkboxes with counts,
  upload-date ranges, reset), searchable tile grid with multi-file and
  drag-and-drop upload, and a persistent inspector for meta editing
  (in the screen's content language, click-to-set focal), the usage
  list, and delete. Kind
  set, committed search, date range, and selected file mirror into the
  query string (`kind`, `q`, `range`, `file`) via
  `history.replaceState`, so the screen state deep-links. Full-page
  island elements carry a `data-cosray-element` marker that `panel.ts`
  loads after the system bridge boots
- removing an asset from a field never deletes the asset; deleting a
  node never blocks on references (backlinks are informational, for the
  panel later)

12) Materialized node titles

- `nodes.title jsonb` is a query-only, denormalized copy of a node's title
  as a locale map (`{locale: text}`, or `{zxx: text}` when not
  language-specific). `Node::title()` stays the authoritative, dynamic
  resolver; the column exists for search, labelling and locale-aware sort
- written at save time in `Node\Store::persist`, folded into the same
  UPDATE/INSERT as the content (one change/history record).
  `Cosray\Title\Resolver` mirrors `title()`'s order: a `Contract\Title`
  node (evaluated once per locale — identical results collapse to the
  neutral `zxx` key), else the schema `titleField`, else a `title` text
  field, else empty. Field titles copy the field's value map verbatim;
  dynamic titles re-hydrate from the content being saved (the passed node
  still holds the previous version)
- locale-aware ordering sorts on the map directly, e.g. `ORDER BY
  COALESCE(NULLIF(title->>'de',''), NULLIF(title->>'zxx','')) COLLATE
  "de-x-icu"` (`Cosray\Title\Sort`), backed by one expression index per
  locale; `php run db:recreate-sort-index` reconciles those indexes
  against the locale keys present in the data (no app boot needed)
- `php run db:titles` (`Cosray\Title\Rebuild`) re-materializes every live
  node's title — the backfill after migration 000000-000022 (which only
  adds the column) and the recovery tool. It needs the booted app (node
  type registry + locales), so an app registers it from its own
  commands.php; the change/history triggers are suspended during the run

Full-text search (complete contract: `docs/fulltext.md`)

- Explicit opt-in only: `#[Fulltext(FulltextWeight::A)]` through D on Text,
  Textarea, RichText, Blocks or Entries. Containers pass weights to supported
  descendants; local weights override and `#[Fulltext(false)]` excludes a
  field/subtree from both matching and snippets. An unselected container can
  still contain explicitly selected children. Custom field types, code, iframe
  markup, identifiers and media are not automatically searchable.
- The resolved computed `Title::title()` implementation may opt in. Its text
  comes from the materialized title map, not a method invocation during
  indexing. Outer/embedded provider precedence is unchanged. Empty effective
  titles contribute nothing and are counted by the rebuild.
- Builder reads flattened schema definitions and stored structured text without
  hydrating nodes or rendering HTML. It honors allowed typed rows, Blocks
  translation modes, owning-scope `When` conditions, locale fallbacks and zxx.
  Unknown rich-text node types are skipped with their subtree, as the renderer
  does.
- One `full_text` row per node/content locale: ordered weighted tsvector plus
  original plain-text `source`. The target locale's analyzer handles the whole
  effective document, including fallback prose. This does not translate queries
  or promise source-language stemming for fallback text.
- `pgDict` names a built-in text-search configuration. Migration 000000-000036
  provisions derived accent-insensitive copies (`fts_<name>`) with unaccent
  ahead of the dictionaries. Missing pgDict uses derived simple; an explicitly
  unavailable name fails when FTS lazily loads configurations before use.
  No runtime DDL; CLI help and migration boot remain database-independent.
- `$cms->nodes()->fulltext($query)->limit(20)->offset($offset)` composes with
  types, filter, hierarchy and counts. Input is bound to websearch_to_tsquery:
  terms AND together, quotes form phrases, OR alternates, minus excludes.
  Empty/punctuation/stopword-only queries match nothing. Negative-only queries
  retain PostgreSQL semantics and may be expensive. No prefix or fuzzy search.
- Default rank is ts_rank_cd, normal A-D weights and normalization 0, then UID
  ascending for stable ties. Explicit order() overrides relevance. Count ignores
  pagination and never evaluates headlines. The DSL identifier fulltext still
  refers to an ordinary content field; search()/searchTitle() are unchanged.
- Public defaults: published, visible, undeleted, with an active usable URL for
  the requested locale/fallback and a routable type. Existing flag toggles are
  inherited; activeUrl(false) separately disables the URL/routability gate.
  Applications must not let client input relax authorization gates. The shared
  index includes selected unpublished, hidden and non-routable live content.
- Fetched wrappers carry readonly Fulltext\Search under meta->search with float
  score and Fulltext\Snippet. Ordinary fetches have no search value; use isset.
  Snippet segments are text/match pairs; text() returns plain text and html()
  escapes all text before adding fixed mark tags. In escaped Boiler use
  `$this->unwrap($node->meta->search->snippet->html())`, never raw ts_headline.
  Highlighting preserves original accents. Fixed bounds: 35 max words, 15 min,
  two fragments separated by an ellipsis. With LIMIT PostgreSQL evaluates
  headlines for limit+offset rows; unlimited results pay per match.
- Store synchronizes live content in the same transaction, using savepoints
  inside an outer transaction. Draft saves/discards keep live text unchanged;
  publishing or folding a working copy reindexes it. Flags/paths are queried
  live; deletion removes documents. Imports bypassing Store need a rebuild.
- App Console\Commands resolves db:fulltext lazily with configured types,
  fields, block registry and locales. Rebuild fetches bounded key batches,
  locks a node before reading, replaces it atomically, reports missing schemas
  and extraction failures, and exits nonzero if incomplete. It changes no
  editorial content/history and disables no triggers. Missing titles are
  reported; after title logic changes run db:titles before db:fulltext.
- Migration 000000-000036 and explicit opt-ins plus a rebuild are required on
  existing apps. Coordinate writes/searches across the deployment/rebuild
  window; row locking alone cannot reconcile different selection/analysis
  policies. Changes to weights, fields, locales, fallbacks or analyzers need
  reindexing. Cosray never truncates to satisfy PostgreSQL's 1 MB vector limit;
  failures name the node/field. PostgreSQL silently clamps positions at 16383.
- Panel FTS, panel-only fields/separate source, class-level defaults, working-copy
  search and ranking customization are deferred. Locale fallback policy and
  the placement of search metadata remain explicit follow-up review topics.

13) Key configuration settings (defaults)

App and environment:

- `app.name`: `env('APP_NAME', 'cosray')` from `$_SERVER`/`$_ENV`; not validated or normalized, so keep it stable and safe for app-specific identifiers
- `app.debug`: `env('APP_DEBUG', false)` from `$_SERVER`/`$_ENV`
- `app.env`: `env('APP_ENV', '')` from `$_SERVER`/`$_ENV`
- `app.secret`: `env('APP_SECRET', null)` from `$_SERVER`/`$_ENV`
- `app.url_prefix`: `''` (application URL mount prefix, e.g. `/site`; exposed as `$config->app->urlPrefix`; never a filesystem prefix). The router applies it to all routes and media URLs include it, but panel-generated links and login redirects do not consistently include non-empty prefixes yet.

Filesystem directories and panel URL paths:

- `path.root`: filesystem root passed to `new Config($root, ...)` or `App::create($root, ...)`
- `path.public`: `$root . '/public'` (filesystem document root)
- `path.assets`: `'/assets'` (uploaded originals below `path.public`, also used as their URL path)
- `path.cache`: `'/cache'` (generated renditions below `path.public`, also used as their URL path; cached icons also live here)
- `path.views`: `'/views'` (view directory relative to `path.root`, despite the leading slash)
- `panel.path`: `'/cp'` (SSR/HTMX panel URL path; exposed as `$config->panel->path`)
- `panel.assets_dir`: `$root . '/panel/static'` (filesystem directory for the built client, exposed as `$config->panel->assetsDir`; `panel:install` writes here and the panel serves it through `{panel.path}/static/...`; changing this directory does not change generated URLs; set `COSRAY_PANEL_DEV=1` to use the Vite dev server)
- `panel.theme`: `[]` (input may be a string or string[] and is exposed as a list through `$config->panel->theme`)
- `panel.logo`: `'/images/logo.png'`
- `panel.dashboard`: `true` (`false` removes the dashboard's masthead entry; the panel root and the logo lead to the first collection, or media)

Errors:

- `error.enabled`: `true` (default error middleware in `Cosray\App`)
- `error.renderer`: `null` (optional `Celema\Core\Error\Renderer` object or class-string)
- `error.trusted`: `[]` (extra trusted classes for Boiler error templates)
- `error.views`: `null` (defaults to `{path.root}{path.views}` plus built-in fallback templates)
- `error.whoops`: `true` (uses `filp/whoops` in debug mode when installed)

Database:

- `db.dsn`: `env('DATABASE_URL', null)` from `$_SERVER`/`$_ENV`
- `db.sql`: `[]`
- `db.migrations`: `[]`
- `db.options`: `[]`
- `db.print`: `false`

Session:

- `session.enabled`: `env('SITE_SESSION_ENABLED', false)` from `$_SERVER`/`$_ENV`; adds session middleware to selected frontend routes
- `session.options.cookie_httponly`: `true`
- `session.options.cookie_lifetime`: `(int) env('SESSION_COOKIE_LIFETIME', '0')`
- `session.options.cookie_secure`: `env('SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE', true)`
- `session.options.gc_maxlifetime`: `(int) env('SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT', '3600')`
- `session.handler`: optional

Uploads and media:

- `upload.maxsize`: `10 * 1024 * 1024`
- `upload.mimetypes.file`: default allows pdf
- `upload.mimetypes.image`: avif, gif, jpeg/jpg/jpe/jfif, png, svg, webp
- `upload.mimetypes.video`: mp4/m4v, ogv/ogg, webm
- `media.fileserver`: `null` or `apache` or `nginx`
- `media.sizes`: `[]` — named rendition sizes (see section 9); built-ins
  `thumb` and `preview` are always available
- `richtext.classes`: `[]` — declared paragraph classes for richtext
  (`'name' => 'Readable label'`, `default` implicit; see section 10)
- `richtext.styles`: `[]` — declared text styles for the `style` mark;
  empty means the mark is unusable

14) Known caveats during exploration

- Keep expectations conservative and verify behavior against `src/` and tests.

attribution:
When possible, cite the exact file path and section used as evidence.
